A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Equivariant Neural Fields work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A-D are readable and can be matched reliably, including material relocated in v5.

before.justification: v4 reports original reconstruction, classification, segmentation and forecasting experiments in Section 4, plus latent-size and shape-conditioning ablations in Appendix D.

after.justification: v5 retains these empirical results and adds original image-generation experiments, component ablations and computational-efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: The core ENF architecture, locality mechanism, kNN approximation and encoding algorithms remain unchanged. Appendix C.4 adds a downstream generative procedure: DiT-B diffuses context vectors while retaining poses, then generates samples using poses drawn from training examples and DDIM denoising. This is a limited procedural extension.

E1.justification: v5 adds unconditional image generation on CIFAR10 and CelebA64×64, substantially extending task coverage beyond reconstruction, classification, segmentation and forecasting. These datasets were already used in v4; the addition concerns task requirements rather than new datasets. Existing coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Table 7 introduces a generative comparison with GEM, GASP and DPF alongside Functa, adding a distinct family of comparison methods. Table 2 also adds NF2vec to ShapeNet16 classification, reporting 93.3% accuracy; v4 included NF2vec only in segmentation comparisons. Existing comparator sets are otherwise retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include FID evaluation using 50,000 generated samples, 200-epoch diffusion training and 512-step sampling; controlled locality and pose-removal experiments; and FLOP, memory and runtime comparisons using three MAML inner steps and batch size 32. Appendix C.2 also confines the previously broadly stated shallow-Functa setting to shape experiments, revising the reported setting without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendices D.2, D.4 and D.5 add substantial tests of Gaussian windowing versus kNN, geometry-free latent sets, and computational costs with and without kNN. The Gaussian-window-only condition remains TBD in Table 9. The original latent-size and shape-information ablations are retained; the transformation visualization is relocated rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. The new generation sample count specifies evaluation size, not repeated experimental runs.

E6.justification: v5 adds ENF generation FIDs of 33.8 on CelebA64×64 and 23.5 on CIFAR10, new locality and pose-removal results, and resource measurements, including 207 seconds per epoch for kNN ENF versus 2864 for Functa. Table 10 reports pose-free accuracy of 47.9%, while its prose says 0.47. Retained benchmark scores and relocated ShapeNet results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix C.4 newly defines the forward diffusion kernel over pose-context latent sets in Equation 9, perturbing contexts while fixing poses. The steerability definition, Lemma 1 and its proof, and Appendix B's bi-invariant formulas remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract extends the claimed empirical validation to generative modelling. The introduction also narrows separation of shape/geometry from appearance to separating aspects of geometry, specifically feature poses. The central steerability, weight-sharing and localized-representation contributions remain intact.

C2.justification: v5 substantially expands mechanism and applicability discussion: kNN is interpreted as implicit windowing, pose-free latent instability is linked to globally coupled optimization, and runtime differences are attributed to architectural depth. It also acknowledges stronger specialist generative methods and instability when diffusing poses, while adding benefits of global latent representations to the introduction.

D1.justification: Appendix C.4 provides substantial new diffusion implementation details, including conditioning, noise schedule, optimizer, training budget and sampling. C.1-C.2 clarify classifier training and disclose Functa's downstream residual MLP; D.5 identifies the profiling procedure. The abstract adds a submission-code repository link alongside the retained minimal repository. Conversely, v4's explicit ShapeNet16 train/test counts are omitted.

R1.justification: v5 explicitly acknowledges earlier steerability results in implicit-shape and equivariant-network research, including Atzmon, Chatzipantazis, Cohen and Bekkers. It adds generative-model and diffusion references and distinguishes generative-objective methods from ENF's representation pretraining. These are targeted attribution and positioning refinements within the retained research framing.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact. v5 expands introductory motivation and attribution, condenses shape-experiment descriptions, adds acknowledgements and appendix subsections, and changes the publication header. The narrative editing is limited despite the added scientific content.

P2.justification: v5 adds generation samples and four new result tables, and substantially reorganizes experimental displays. The full ShapeNet segmentation table and examples move to Appendix D.6, with a compact summary replacing the main-text table. The transformation figure moves from v4 Figure 6 to v5 Figure 10. Existing figure imagery is retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v4, v5 provides more direct component tests and measured computational costs supporting its locality and efficiency arguments, alongside clearer attribution and implementation information. These improve the paper's evidential support. However, Table 9 leaves an important ablation condition TBD, the new pose-free accuracy is inconsistent between prose and Table 10, and ShapeNet16 split counts disappear. These reporting weaknesses limit the overall quality gain.
